in_arabic.name: سوهبة
in_arabic.meaning: اسم يعني هبة من الله، منة، وإحسان، تطلق على المؤنث
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم سوهبة مشتق من الفعل وهب، ويعني الهدية أو العطاء بدون مقابل، ويدل على الإحسان والكرم، وتسمى به المرأة كتعبير عن امتنانها لله على نعمه، ووردت مشتقاته في القرآن الكريم في سياق الحديث عن نعم الله على عباده، مثل قوله تعالى:  وَيَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَاءُ الذُّكُورَ أَوَ الإِنَاثَ أَوَ الْمُضَاعَفَ

in_urdu.name: سوبھا
in_urdu.meaning: سوبھا نام کا مطلب ہے اللہ کی طرف سے عطا کردہ نعمت
in_urdu.long_meaning: سوبھا نام عربی زبان کے الفاظ سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے ہبہ یا تحفہ، یہ نام اس عظیم احساس کو ظاہر کرتا ہے جو اللہ کی طرف سے ملنے والی نعمتوں کی قدر کرنے کے لیے ہے، اور یہ جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی روایت میں ایک مقبول نام ہے جو لڑکیوں کو دیا جاتا ہے

It is derived from the Arabic word 'Sohibah', which means 'one who is bestowed with a precious gift'. This name is often given to a child who is born in a family after a long wait or after several miscarriages or stillbirths. The name carries the belief that the child is a precious gift from Allah and is a source of blessing and joy for the family.

The name is a reminder that each person has been bestowed with talents, abilities, and opportunities, which make them valuable and essential to the world. By embracing this truth, one can develop a deep sense of self-worth and purpose, and live a life that is meaningful and fulfilling. Furthermore, the name encourages the individual to strive towards excellence in all aspects of life, as a way of expressing gratitude for the blessings of Allah. The name Sohiba ultimately serves as a powerful reminder of the interconnectedness of all things and the importance of being grateful for the gifts that Allah has bestowed upon us.

historical_references.context: Sohiba is a common name given to revered female figures in Islamic history. It is believed to originate from the Arabic word 'shafa' meaning 'to relieve' or 'to help'. Shaikh Abdul Qadir Jilani is one such historical figure who carried this name.

historical_references.reference: Sohiba is also the name of a significant female figure in the history of the Mughal Empire. She was the mother of the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan (1592-1666 AD) and was renowned for her beauty and grace. Her real name was Arjumand Banu Begum.
historical_references.context: The name 'Sohiba' is not only associated with Sufi saints but also with other esteemed women in Islamic history.
